Today's TL;DRRegimeMIXED
Markets are caught in a tug-of-war between a hawkish Fed repricing driven by Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole comments (raising rate-hike odds, lifting yields, and pressuring gold) and a booming AI capex supercycle anchored by Nvidia's explosive earnings and data-center buildout. Trade war escalation with Canada, rare-earth tensions with China, and social-media litigation add downside risk, while a US-Venezuela oil deal and potential US-Iran diplomacy offer geopolitical offsets. The regime is MIXED: fixed income and some commodities are bearish, equities are split (tech bullish, consumer/regulatory bearish), and crypto sees institutional inflows but systemic warnings.

AI Infrastructure Capex SurgeAI基础设施资本支出激增
×11 · 44 steps
Hyperscaler and sovereign AI capex is surging, with top 4 CSPs capex up 87% YoY in 2Q26 and US hyperscaler capex projected at $940bn. AI and technology investment remains fundamentally strong despite macro headwinds. Compute supply growth continues to lag demand for AI services, with MiniMax's training utilization reaching 97% in 1H26 and Goldman Sachs expecting the imbalance to persist through 2028; Morgan Stanley estimates SpaceX's $100bn Starbase LA facility represents only 2% of total capex given AI spending scale, funded partly by ~$80bn/yr net debt issuance.

China Domestic Demand Weakness中国内需疲软
×10 · 39 steps
Chinese consumer demand remains persistently weak, with retail sales growth stagnating at 0-1% YoY, new vehicle sales down ~20% YoY, and industrial production capacity utilization at 73% in 2Q26. Despite Politburo and State Council pledges, China economic activity remains weak: property transactions down -13.5% yoy, steel demand -5.6% yoy, steel production -10.5% yoy, coal consumption -3.9% yoy (R471). This weakness is echoed in company results: Gongniu Group cited industry weakness (R467) and Ningbo Tuopu saw its air suspension market share drop from 37.4% to 27.4% and GPM decline -1.5pp yoy amid customer pricing pressure and raw material cost inflation (R472).

Middle East Conflict and Energy Supply Disruption中东冲突与能源供应中断
×8 · 35 steps
US-Iran conflict is driving volatility in energy prices and supply chains. Strait of Hormuz disruptions reduced crude exports from ~15 mb/d to ~6 mb/d. Brent at ~$94/bbl despite disruption absorbed by stockpiling and supplier diversification. Ongoing Middle East disruptions continue to propagate globally: limited LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz keep 3Q26 US-to-Asia net gas spreads near $14.80/mmbtu and 4Q26-4Q27 strip spreads up ~40%, while Middle East logistics disruptions also drive MLCC sales shortfalls and a likely decline in Taiyo Yuden's 1.72 book-to-bill ratio.

    Conclusion
    If prime-age LFPRs stall at their July rates, they will end this year about ½ point below last December—straining labor supply and pushing down the unemployment rate. For scale: a 1 point decline in prime-age LFPR subtracts about ½ point from the overall LFPR; the breakeven pace for payrolls has been running at about 50k per month; if prime-age LFPR falls at a pace that would lower it a point over the course of a year, the breakeven pace would fall to slightly below zero, and the unemployment rate would likely fall slightly below 4.0% by year end given current payroll forecasts.
    b98e935b7ed4·《Recent declines in labor force participation》·2026-08-23

    Premise

    656bf28703d0·《Hot Chips Day 1: Key Themes and Takeaways》·2026-08-29
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The CPU role is evolving toward orchestration, data movement, scheduling, and agent coordination across Intel, AMD, Nvidia, Fujitsu, and Arm; Nvidia said agentic AI is a workflow problem, not just a compute problem, and Vera CPU is explicitly designed to maximize agent performance per core, data processing, and I/O; Fujitsu said agentic AI increases CPU demand for orchestration and peripheral processing; Intel Wildcat Lake was designed to handle AI orchestration through its NPU and CPU cores.
    656bf28703d0·《Hot Chips Day 1: Key Themes and Takeaways》·2026-08-29
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    AI system performance is increasingly limited by memory bandwidth, interconnects, and data movement rather than pure compute; Nvidia Rubin GPU has scalable coherency architecture, massive I/O, NVLink 6 with 3x lower latency and 10x higher packet rate versus Ethernet; AMD MI455X has 432GB HBM4 and 23.3 TB/s bandwidth; Intel Diamond Rapids has 16-channel memory architecture and unified memory fabric.
    656bf28703d0·《Hot Chips Day 1: Key Themes and Takeaways》·2026-08-29

Thresholds calibrated on a single event — the 2026-06/07 semiconductor selloff (n=1)
Trigger rule details
The three observed quantities
Sector relative strength = how far a sector's return has beaten the broad market's over the trailing quarter (a price proxy for crowding)
Market breadth = how many stocks participate in the rally (equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight = narrowing breadth)
% above 200-day MA = how far price sits above its own 200-day moving average (the standard BIAS technical indicator)
How the light is decided
🔴 Red: hottest sector's relative strength enters the top 5% of 10 years (≥95) AND market breadth narrows into the top 10% (≥90) — both must hold
🟡 Amber: relative strength ≥95 but breadth only to ≥60; or either relative strength or 200-day bias enters the top 1% (≥99)
🟢 Green: everything else
Once red has fired, it doesn't snap straight back to green: it must exit the top 20% (relative strength) or the top 60% (breadth) before returning to green, resting on amber in between (anti-flicker)
Any missing data shows “No data” — it never defaults to green
